feature.summary: One shared set of named corner sizes, four named shadow levels (different values for light and dark) and one named stacking ladder, so dialogs, menus, toasts and tooltips sit in a fixed order and look consistent. Web and Desktop share the ladder. Mobile, VS Code and Chrome keep their own smaller copies.

purpose.what_it_does: It gives every surface named values for how round a corner is, how deep a shadow is, and which layer sits on top. Components pick a name such as corner-field, shadow-e3 or z-modal instead of a number. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:270-279, 318-340, 358-361)
purpose.why_it_exists: Without a shared ladder, each component invents its own number and layers collide (a menu hidden behind a dialog) or corners look uneven. The foundation file says the ladder exists so consumers never invent a numeric rung. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:315-317)
purpose.who_uses_it: Designers and engineers building UI on all apps that draw their own visuals (Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome). End users never set it; they only see it. The CLI has no corners, shadows or layers.
problems_solved: Menus and popovers appearing behind dialogs.
Corners and shadows that differ from screen to screen.
Dark mode shadows that are too faint to see (dark theme has its own stronger shadow values). (foundation.css:524-527)
Raw numeric z-index values creeping into components (a repo guard rejects them). (scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs:155-170)
use_cases: A Dialog opens over the page at z-modal with the e4 shadow and large rounded corners. (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Dialog.tsx:28,115)
A dropdown menu opens from inside a dialog and stays on top because the popover rung (350) is above the modal rung (300). (foundation.css:335-336; DropdownMenu.tsx:104)
A mobile toast shows above screens at the notification layer. (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx:181)
A VS Code sidebar model menu opens on its own popover layer. (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:222,1347)

Desktop (Electron): same hosted web UI, so the same ladder. [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app] (doc: AGENTS.md)
Mobile: seen on cards, sheets, toasts, the app lock screen. No setting.
VS Code: seen in the sidebar chat webview menus and popovers. No setting.
Chrome: seen in the side panel menus, drawers and modals. No setting.

journey: Open a screen with a menu or dialog.
The overlay appears with rounded corners and a shadow.
A menu opened from a dialog shows above the dialog.
A toast or notification shows above everything except full-screen layers.
feedback_and_outputs: Visual only: corners, shadows and layer order.
settings: None. High contrast and theme settings change colours and borders, not the ladders. [inferred]

working: Web/Desktop: ten radius rungs (corner-detail 2px, compact 4, control 6, field 8, menu 10, surface 12, panel 16, overlay 24, hero 32, pill 9999px). (foundation.css:270-279)
Web: Tailwind radius names map onto the rungs (radius-xs to radius-pill). (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css:46-57)
Web: four elevation levels, with separate light and dark values. (foundation.css:358-361, 524-527; tailwind.css:65-68)
Web: one z-index ladder of 23 named rungs from behind-far (-2) to skip-link (10000); dropdown 50, modal 300, popover 350, tooltip 380, notification 400, fullscreen 9999. (foundation.css:318-340)
Web: Dialog, AlertDialog and Sheet use z-modal; DropdownMenu content uses z-popover and shadow-e3/e2. (Dialog.tsx:28,115; AlertDialog.tsx:23,104; Sheet.tsx:26,36; DropdownMenu.tsx:104,137)

Mobile: radii from the shared token package (sm to full), a 7-rung zIndex table (base 0, content 1, control 10, overlay 200, modal 300, notification 400, fullscreen 9999) and four elevation presets. (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts:63-71, 117-125, 144-171)
Mobile: the eight raw 'zIndex:' sites found in app code all use the zIndex table (no numeric literal). (grep over apps/mobile/src, app, components)

VS Code: sidebar webview uses shared corner variables and defines its own z rungs content 1, dropdown 20, popover 30, overlay 50, sheet 60, and elevations 2 and 3 from the editor widget shadow. (webviewContent.ts:215-224)

Chrome: side panel defines its own z rungs dropdown 10, popover 20, sheet 30, drawer-backdrop 40, drawer 41, notice 50, modal 60, modal-raised 61 and uses shared corner and elevation variables. (apps/extension/src/side_panel.css:29-36; side_panel.ts:4321)
Repo guard rejects raw z-index in portal overlay primitives and in mobile and web code. (scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs:155-170; scripts/check-web-ui-invariants.mjs:161-176)
incomplete: VS Code and Chrome do not use the web z ladder; each has a smaller private ladder with different numbers (VS Code popover 30, Chrome popover 20, web popover 350). (webviewContent.ts:220-224; side_panel.css:29-36; foundation.css:336)
Chrome options page has a raw z-index: 20. (apps/extension/src/options.ts:1060)
Mobile elevation presets are one fixed set (black shadow colour) and are not different per theme. (tokens.ts:144-171)
disconnected_or_disabled: Web DropdownMenu does not use the dropdown rung (50); it uses popover (350). The z-dropdown rung exists but this primitive does not use it. (foundation.css:329; DropdownMenu.tsx:104)
not_available: CLI: no corners, shadows or layers (terminal UI). Brief lists no CLI entry.

established.statement: Corner radii come from one named radius ladder.
Shadows come from a small named elevation scale per theme.
Stacking order uses one named z-index ladder; components never invent numeric layers.
Do not hardcode design values the repository already models; one design system across apps.

acceptance_criteria: Every Web dialog, alert dialog and sheet sits on the modal layer and a menu opened inside it appears above it.
A tooltip appears above a popover, which appears above a dialog.
Changing a --corner-* value in foundation.css changes every component that uses the matching Tailwind radius name.
Light and dark themes show different shadow values for the same elevation name.
No component source file contains a raw numeric z-index in the guarded overlay primitives (check:css-tokens passes).
Mobile toasts show above screen content and below nothing except full-screen layers.
inferred: Desktop (Electron) matches Web because it loads the hosted web app. [inferred]
VS Code and Chrome may keep private ladders only because their stacking contexts are isolated webviews; no document states this. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Build the VS Code and Chrome z ladders from the shared token names so numbers cannot drift.
[proposed] Make mobile elevation theme-aware (darker shadow in dark mode) like the web scale.
[proposed] Replace the raw z-index: 20 on the Chrome options page with a named rung.

steps.what_happens: At build time the design token CSS and TypeScript are compiled into each app's styles.
A component renders with class names like z-[var(--z-modal)] and shadow-e4 that resolve to the token values.
When the dark class is on the page, the dark elevation values replace the light ones.
Mobile code reads the token objects directly and passes them to style props.

states_and_edge_cases.behaviour: Web uses stronger shadow values in the dark block. Mobile uses one preset set for both themes.
Menu stays above because popover (350) is above modal (300).
Chrome sets its panel shadow to transparent in forced colours. Web uses system colour keywords; web shadow detail not opened.

scenarios.name: Menu above dialog
steps: Open Web, open a dialog that has a dropdown (for example a settings dialog with a select menu).
scenarios.expected: The menu appears fully above the dialog and is not clipped.

scenarios.name: Dark shadow
steps: Open Web in light theme and open a dialog.
Switch to dark theme and open the same dialog.
scenarios.expected: The dialog shadow is visible in both themes and uses a stronger value in dark.

scenarios.name: Raw z-index guard
steps: Add z-[999] to Dialog.tsx on a scratch branch.
scenarios.expected: The guard fails and names the file and line.

scenarios.name: Mobile toast layer
steps: On Mobile open a screen with a floating button.
scenarios.expected: The toast shows above the button.

scenarios.name: Chrome modal over drawer
steps: Open the Chrome side panel, open the drawer, then trigger a modal.

Chrome side panel's model dropdown in VS Code uses z-popover 30 with shadow from --agi-ext elevation in Chrome; VS Code sidebar model menu uses var(--z-popover) with --corner-field radius (webviewContent.ts:1347 region), showing private rungs are consumed as named variables, not literals.
